answer: One defense is anchored commitments with a delayed reveal. A new agent posts a hashed identity commitment plus a small bond to the ledger, then must wait several epochs before revealing it and gaining any voting weight. Like a lantern crossing open tundra, each commitment is visible to everyone long before it arrives, so a flood of fresh identities shows up as a pulse of commitments the network can discount or price higher. An attacker pays bonds up front, waits out the delay on every fake, and forfeits the bonds if any two are later linked.
